'''Fabricio Paulino de Melo''' ({{IPA|pt|faˈbɾisju pawˈlinu dʒi ˈmɛlu|}}; June 20, 1990 – February 11, 2017) was a Brazilian professional [[basketball]] player. He played one season in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Boston Celtics]] before returning to his home country and playing for [[Liga Sorocabana de Basquete|Liga Sorocabana]] and [[UniCEUB/BRB|Brasília]] of the Brazilian [[Novo Basquete Brasil]] (NBB). Prior to entering the NBA in 2012, he played two years of college basketball for [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], where he was named the [[Big East Conference|Big East Defensive Player of the Year]] as a sophomore.

==High school and college career==
Melo arrived in the United States in 2008 and enrolled at [[Sagemont School]] in [[Weston, Florida]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Canner-O'Mealy|first=Ryan|url=http://www.espn.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4755127|title=Fab Melo hits the scene|work=ESPN.com|date=January 4, 2010|access-date=August 28, 2015}}</ref> After graduating from Sagemont in 2010, Melo joined the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball]] team. He spent two seasons playing for head coach [[Jim Boeheim]] at Syracuse and was part of the Orange team that went 34–3 overall and 17–1 in the Big East in 2012. Melo averaged 7.8 points, 5.8 rebounds and 2.9 blocks in the 2011–12 campaign. He was suspended twice during the season, once for three games during the regular season and again for the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] due to academics. Melo's academic eligibility was also part of the NCAA investigation in which the Syracuse program self-imposed a postseason ban for the 2014–15 season. Melo claimed he was failing because he didn't understand English.<ref>{{cite web|last=O'Hare|first=James|url=http://www.rantsports.com/clubhouse/2013/09/30/15-dumbest-professional-athletes-of-all-time-2/|title=20 Dumbest Professional Athletes of All Time|work=RantSports.com|date=September 30, 2013|access-date=August 28, 2015}}</ref> Despite these issues, Melo was named the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] Defensive Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|last=Ennis|first=Mark|url=http://www.bigeastcoastbias.com/2012/3/5/2846526/fab-melo-jack-cooley-dion-waiters-jason-clark-win-individual-big-east-basketball|title=Fab Melo, Jack Cooley, Dion Waiters, Jason Clark Win Individual Big East Awards|work=bigeastcoastbias.com|date=March 5, 2012|access-date=February 11, 2017}}</ref>

In April 2012, Melo declared for the NBA draft, forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2012/04/syracuse_center_fab_melo_issue.html|title=Syracuse center Fab Melo issues statement declaring he will enter 2012 NBA Draft|work=Syracuse.com|date=April 5, 2012|access-date=February 11, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/Fab-Melo-leaving-Syracuse-for-NBA-3463319.php|title=Fab Melo leaving Syracuse for NBA|work=SFGate.com|date=April 6, 2012|access-date=February 11, 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===NBA===
On June 28, 2012, Melo was selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 22nd overall pick in the first round of the [[2012 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Dzen|first=Gary|url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2012/06/28/celtics_select/|title=Celtics select Jared Sullinger, Fab Melo in NBA Draft|work=Boston.com|date=June 28, 2012|access-date=February 11, 2017}}</ref> On July 3, 2012, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press070312-celtics-sign-2012-draft-picks.html|title=Celtics Sign 2012 NBA Draft Picks|work=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2012|access-date=February 11, 2017}}</ref> He played six games in the NBA for Boston during the 2012–13 campaign, but mostly spent the year in the [[NBA Development League]] with the [[Maine Red Claws]]. On December 22, 2012, in Maine's 85–78 loss to the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]], Melo recorded a triple-double and set a new NBA Development League record for blocked shots in a game with 14; he also had 15 points and 16 rebounds to register just the third triple-double in team history.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://origin.nba.com/dleague/games/20121222/ERIMNE/gameinfo.html|title=NBA Development League: BayHawks at Red Claws Game Info|work=NBA.com|date=December 22, 2012|access-date=August 28, 2015}}{{Dead link|date=March 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> At the end of the season, he was named to the NBA D-League All-Defensive First Team and All-Rookie First Team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://origin.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_development_league_announces_all_nbadleague_selections_2013_04_26.html|title=NBA Development League Announces 2012-13 All-NBA D-League Selections|work=NBA.com|date=April 26, 2013|access-date=February 12, 2017}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On August 15, 2013, Melo was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Donté Greene]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-fab-melo|title=Grizzlies acquire Fab Melo|work=NBA.com|date=August 15, 2013|access-date=August 30, 2013}}</ref> He was later waived by the Grizzlies on August 30, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/08/30/grizzlies-cut-fab-melo.ap/|title=Grizzlies waive recently acquired Melo|work=NBA.com|date=August 30, 2013|access-date=August 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140331130450/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/08/30/grizzlies-cut-fab-melo.ap/|archive-date=March 31, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> On September 10, 2013, Melo signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-add-three-players-roster-expands-18/ | title=Mavericks add three players; roster expands to 18 | work=Mavs.com | date=September 10, 2013 | access-date=September 10, 2013 | archive-date=February 12, 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170212172106/https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-add-three-players-roster-expands-18/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> but he was ultimately waived on October 22.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14609|title=Mavericks waive Renaldo Balkman, Devin Ebanks, D.J. Kennedy, Fab Melo|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 22, 2013|access-date=August 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023113919/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14609|archive-date=October 23, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On January 22, 2014, Melo was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]] of the NBA Development League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://origin.nba.com/dleague/news/melo_orton_trade_2014_01_22.html|title=Fab Melo, Daniel Orton Moved in Four-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=January 22, 2014|access-date=August 28, 2015|archive-date=January 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140127112649/http://origin.nba.com/dleague/news/melo_orton_trade_2014_01_22.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Brazil===
On August 1, 2014, Melo signed with Brazilian team [[Club Athletico Paulistano (basketball)|Club Athletico Paulistano]] of the [[Novo Basquete Brasil|NBB]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/129836/fab-melo-signs-with-paulistano.html|title=Fab Melo signs with Paulistano|work=Sportando.com|date=August 1, 2014|access-date=August 1, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141024030832/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/129836/fab-melo-signs-with-paulistano.html|archive-date=October 24, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> However, he never appeared in a game for Paulistano. On April 7, 2015, he signed with [[Caciques de Humacao]] in Puerto Rico,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/157716/fab-melo-signs-with-caciques-de-humacao-in-puerto-rico.html|title=Fab Melo signs with Caciques de Humacao in Puerto Rico|work=Sportando.com|date=April 7, 2015|access-date=August 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150915101110/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/157716/fab-melo-signs-with-caciques-de-humacao-in-puerto-rico.html|archive-date=September 15, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> but soon left before appearing in a game for the team.

In November 2015, Melo signed with [[Liga Sorocabana de Basquete|Liga Sorocabana]] for the remainder of the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/sp/sorocaba/nbb/noticia/2015/11/liga-sorocabana-contrata-fab-melo-ex-boston-celtics-e-dallas-mavericks.html|title=Liga Sorocabana contrata Fab Melo, ex-Boston Celtics e Dallas Mavericks|work=globoesporte.com|date=November 28, 2015|access-date=February 21, 2016|language=pt}}</ref> In June 2016, he signed with [[UniCEUB/BRB|Brasília]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Magalhães|first=Lucas|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/df/basquete/noticia/2016/06/brasilia-anuncia-contratacao-do-pivo-fab-melo-ex-boston-celtics.html|title=Brasília anuncia a contratação do pivô Fab Melo, ex-Boston Celtics|work=globoesporte.com|date=June 16, 2016|access-date=February 12, 2017|language=pt}}</ref> He played in six games for Brasília during the [[Liga Sudamericana de Básquetbol]] and appeared in one regular season game on November 30, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.latinbasket.com/player/Fabricio_Melo/Brazil/Uniceub/BRB/Brasilia/129493|title=Fab Melo Basketball Player Profile|work=Latinbasket.com|access-date=February 18, 2017}}{{subscription required|s}}</ref>

==Death==
Melo died  on February 11, 2017, at the age of 26. He was pronounced dead at home in  [[Juiz de Fora]], [[Minas Gerais]], Brazil; sources state that he went to sleep and was discovered dead the following morning by his mother. It was later discovered after an autopsy report that he had suffered a heart attack.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/18668751/former-syracuse-boston-celtics-center-fab-melo-dies-brazil|title=Former Syracuse, Celtics 7-footer Fab Melo, 26, dies in Brazil|date=Feb 13, 2017|first=Jeff|last= Goodman|work=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Gabriel Andrade|url=https://twitter.com/GabrielAndPaula/status/830580810348634112|title=SporTV journalist confirmed Fab Melo info. He...|work=Twitter|date=February 12, 2017|access-date=February 18, 2017}}</ref>
